## Comparability note

Alaska Air Group's FY2024 revenue is not directly comparable to its FY2022/FY2023 revenue: Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward [DOC-2]. Per the disclosure, Hawaiian contributed $869 million of revenue from the acquisition date through December 31, 2024 [DOC-2], so I subtract that amount from Alaska's FY2024 reported revenue of $11,735M [DOC-1] to get an organic (legacy Alaska) FY2024 revenue of $10,866M. Note this is a partial-period figure only — it removes ~3.5 months of Hawaiian, not a full year — so Alaska's adjusted growth is a same-perimeter comparison against FY2022/FY2023, but on a full-year pro forma basis Hawaiian's contribution would be larger. The other four carriers are all calendar-year filers with no comparability adjustment noted [DOC-1].

## FY2023 → FY2024 revenue growth

| Rank | Airline | FY2023 | FY2024 | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | United | $53,717M | $57,063M | **+6.23%** [DOC-1] |
| 2 | Delta | $58,048M | $61,643M | +6.19% [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Southwest | $26,091M | $27,483M | +5.34% [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $10,426M | $10,866M | +4.22% [DOC-1][DOC-2] |
| 5 | American | $52,788M | $54,211M | +2.70% [DOC-1] |

(Alaska as reported, including Hawaiian, would be +12.55%, i.e., first place — the ranking is entirely driven by the acquisition adjustment.)

## FY2022 → FY2024 revenue growth

| Rank | Airline | FY2022 | FY2024 | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | United | $44,955M | $57,063M | **+26.93%** [DOC-1] |
| 2 | Delta | $50,582M | $61,643M | +21.87% [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Southwest | $23,814M | $27,483M | +15.41% [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $9,646M | $10,866M | +12.65% [DOC-1][DOC-2] |
| 5 | American | $48,971M | $54,211M | +10.70% [DOC-1] |

## Conclusion

Yes — United Airlines Holdings ranks first in both periods. The one-year margin over Delta is only about 3 basis points (6.23% vs. 6.19%), so the FY2023→FY2024 top spot is effectively a tie; the two-year ranking is decisive (26.9% vs. 21.9%).

ANSWER: Yes — United ranks first in both. FY23→FY24: United +6.23%, Delta +6.19%, Southwest +5.34%, Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) +4.22%, American +2.70%. FY22→FY24: United +26.93%, Delta +21.87%, Southwest +15.41%, Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) +12.65%, American +10.70%.
